# The Clifford group is generated by $H$, $S$ and CNOT

Let $n \ge 1$ and let $U$ be a unitary on $n$ qubits in the Clifford group, so $U \mathcal{P}_n U^{*} = \mathcal{P}_n$.
Then $U = e^{i\theta} G_1 G_2 \cdots G_m$ for some $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, where each $G_j$ is a Hadamard gate $H$ or a
phase gate $S = \operatorname{diag}(1, i)$ on one qubit, or a CNOT gate on an ordered pair of distinct qubits, tensored
with the identity on the other qubits.

Gottesman's construction is by induction on $n$. After a one-qubit Clifford gate and a swap,
$U Z_1 U^{*} = X_1 \otimes M'$ and $U X_1 U^{*} = I \otimes N'$ or $Z_1 \otimes N'$ for Pauli operators $M', N'$ on the other
qubits. Measuring $Z_1$ after $U$ shows $U(|0\rangle |\psi\rangle) = (I + U Z_1 U^{*})(|0\rangle \otimes U' |\psi\rangle)$ for an
$(n-1)$-qubit Clifford unitary $U'$; then $U$ equals $U'$ on the last qubits, followed by $N'$ controlled on qubit $1$, a
Hadamard on qubit $1$, and $M'$ controlled on qubit $1$. Controlled Pauli operators and one- and two-qubit Clifford
gates are products of $H$, $S$ and CNOT. For $n + 1 \ge 3$ qubits the construction uses at most $2(n - 2)$ one-qubit and
$n^2 + n - 1$ two-qubit Clifford gates.
